title: Cour des comptes audit traces undisclosed tranches in Fonds souverain accounts
content: A draft audit by the Cour des comptes, examined by this newspaper, identifies at least nine tranches of the Fonds souverain des Républiques that were placed between 2022 and 2025 through intermediary companies registered in Vallonne, for a cumulative amount of **6.4 billion livres**.

The report, which is expected to be published in redacted form next month, describes a pattern: tranches approved by the fund’s investment committee with minimal documentation, then redirected to entities whose beneficial owners are not disclosed in the register of the Ministry of Finance. In four cases, the auditors could not establish the final destination of the funds.
img::/gazette/images/5/redacted-documents.webp::Les documents du Fonds souverain remis à la Cour des comptes, en partie occultés. Photographie : ADR.

The auditors also criticise the fund’s internal controls, noting that the *déontologie* rules adopted in 2023 were never translated into operational procedures. They recommend the suspension of two senior officials pending an administrative inquiry, and a complete restatement of the fund’s quarterly reporting.

The ministry declined to comment, citing the secret de l’instruction now applied to the parallel inquiry at the Parquet général. The board of the Fonds souverain, chaired by Léon Basty, issued a statement denying any irregularity and describing the preliminary findings as “based on incomplete documents”.

Publication of the draft places added pressure on the Assemblée des Républiques, whose commission des finances was already scheduled to hold hearings on the fund next week. Two members of the commission said the audit would change the scope of those hearings, and that the governor of the Banque des Républiques would now be heard in public session.

Independent analysts note that the sums at issue are small relative to the fund’s 480 billion livres in assets, but that the significance lies in the governance failure. “The market can absorb 6.4 billion; it cannot absorb the discovery that nobody was checking,” said an economist who advises two institutional investors.

The Cour des comptes is expected to submit its final observations to the fund’s board within three weeks. Under the rules of procedure, the board has a right of response, and its answer will be published alongside the final report.
author: Théodore Marchetti, enquête économique — Agence Économique d’Aurelle (AEA)
